rootCauses.what: The 3D Ember Warden was rendered in WebGL every frame, read back with a synchronous gl.readPixels (GPU pipeline stall), then run through three 47k-pixel JS loops (TBDR sanitize flood fill, ink outline/crease/tint, foot shadow projection) and putImageData before being drawn into the hero canvas.
rootCauses.fix: All passes moved to the GPU: copyFramebufferToTexture + a fragment-shader port of the ink/crease/tint pass, and the foot-anchored shadow ported to 4 GPU passes (per-column foot line, sole/base-line params, point scatter with MAX blending + contact ellipses, 3x3 feather) written below the sprite in the same WebGL canvas. No readback remains.

rootCauses.what: Each live NixieFX particle costs ~14us of main-thread time on the phone (regression over 1959 frames); a level-8 fight peaks near 1000 particles, mostly decorative hit sparks and flame-fan impacts that are exempt from per-effect caps.
rootCauses.fix: Adaptive particle budget in src/fx/stage.ts: on devices that cannot hold ~50+ fps while particles are live, the budget shrinks (min 260) and secondary bursts (hit sparks except incoming, impacts, cast/swing ground glows) are skipped when they would exceed it. Casts, bolts, detonations, telegraphs, level-up and incoming-hit feedback always play. Devices holding 60 fps keep full VFX.

benchmark.note: Headless SwiftShader (software GPU, 2D canvas not accelerated) on a loaded 10-core host; JS phases are the meaningful numbers, total frame time is GPU-emulation bound.

telemetry: Tracelogs now carry phasesAvg/phasesMax/frames hero3dMs and vfxMs (sub-phases of encountersRender) and scene.particleBudget.
